html:
The Guasave were an Indigenous people of the coast of northern Sinaloa in Mexico, around the lower Sinaloa River and the present town of Guasave. The Tamazula seem to have been a related group nearby.

They lived by fishing, gathering shellfish and salt, and some farming, and were noted by the Spanish for their warlike reputation. Jesuit missions reached them from the 1590s. Their language is poorly recorded; it may have been related to those of the Cáhita peoples to the north or the Tahue to the south. Like most small peoples of the coast, they had merged into the general population by the 1700s.
